newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends lower in wait-and-see mood.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends lower in wait-and-see mood.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed Wednesday slightly down in thin trade, with investors adopting a wait-and-see stance while listed companies prepare their interim reports, brokers said.
The index inched down 0.09 points or 0.06 percent to 132.73 points as turnover shrank to HK$39 million from Tuesday's HK$56 million.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index slipped 3.64 points or 0.88 percent to 409.59 on turnover of 7.1 billion yuan against Tuesday's 7.0 billion.
"The B index fell in narrow-band fluctuation while investors poked around for fresh talk about the company reports," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Buyers were concentrating on companies expected to post strong profits in their first-half 1997 reports as the August 30 deadline for listed firms to publish interim results drew near, analysts said.
"Trading (in B shares) was quiet today and I expect a further modest correction ahead," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
Brokers said the markets were trending steadily upwards in the medium term on slight optimism over the interim results and general confidence in China's economy.
"But I don't think the indices will surge to spectacular heights because people know what the government will do if the markets are overheated," the China Southern analyst said.
Beijing began in May to roll out a series of hard-hitting policies aimed at curbing excessive speculative stock trading.
Colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics Co Ltd was the biggest B share loser and slumped HK$0.28 or 8.54 percent to HK$3.00.
In the A share market, Fujian-based construction contractor China Wuyi Co Ltd was the worst performer and lost 1.18 yuan or 8.36 percent to 12.94 yuan.
